passages.text: Now the Philistines gathered their forces for war at Socoh in Judah, and they camped between Socoh and Azekah in Ephes-dammim.
passages.sermon:
The Philistines were Israel’s enemies.
The Philistines gathered their army for war.
They gathered at Socoh.
Socoh was a town in Judah.
The Philistines set up camp.
They camped between Socoh and Azekah.
They camped in a place called Ephes-dammim.
passages.original: וַיַּאַסְפ֨וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֤ים אֶת־ מַֽחֲנֵיהֶם֙ לַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וַיֵּאָ֣סְפ֔וּ שֹׂכֹ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר לִיהוּדָ֑ה וַֽיַּחֲנ֛וּ בֵּין־ שׂוֹכֹ֥ה וּבֵין־ עֲזֵקָ֖ה בְּאֶ֥פֶס דַּמִּֽים׃

passages.text: Saul and the men of Israel assembled and camped in the Valley of Elah, arraying themselves for battle against the Philistines.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
The men of Israel followed Saul.
Saul and the men of Israel gathered together.
They camped in the Valley of Elah.
They prepared for battle.
They set themselves in order to fight the Philistines.
passages.original: וְשָׁא֤וּל וְאִֽישׁ־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ נֶאֶסְפ֔וּ וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּעֵ֣מֶק הָאֵלָ֑ה וַיַּעַרְכ֥וּ מִלְחָמָ֖ה לִקְרַ֥את פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃

passages.text: The Philistines stood on one hill and the Israelites stood on another, with the valley between them.
passages.sermon: The Philistines stood on one hill.\r\nThe Israelites stood on another hill.\r\nA valley lay between them.
passages.original: וּפְלִשְׁתִּ֞ים עֹמְדִ֤ים אֶל־ הָהָר֙ מִזֶּ֔ה וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל עֹמְדִ֥ים אֶל־ הָהָ֖ר מִזֶּ֑ה וְהַגַּ֖יְא בֵּינֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Then a champion named Goliath, who was from Gath, came out from the Philistine camp. He was six cubits and a span in height, and he had a bronze helmet on his head. He wore a bronze coat of mail weighing five thousand shekels, and he had armor of bronze on his legs and a javelin of bronze slung between his shoulders.
passages.sermon:
A man came out from the Philistine camp.
His name was Goliath.
Goliath was from Gath.
Goliath was a champion.
Goliath was very tall.
He stood six cubits and a span in height.
Goliath wore a bronze helmet on his head.
He wore a coat of mail made of bronze.
The coat of mail weighed five thousand shekels.
Goliath had bronze armor on his legs.
He carried a bronze javelin slung between his shoulders.
passages.original: וַיֵּצֵ֤א אִֽישׁ־ הַבֵּנַ֙יִם֙ מִמַּחֲנ֣וֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים גָּלְיָ֥ת שְׁמ֖וֹ מִגַּ֑ת גָּבְה֕וֹ שֵׁ֥שׁ אַמּ֖וֹת וָזָֽרֶת׃ וְכ֤וֹבַע נְחֹ֙שֶׁת֙ עַל־ רֹאשׁ֔וֹ וְשִׁרְי֥וֹן קַשְׂקַשִּׂ֖ים ה֣וּא לָב֑וּשׁ וּמִשְׁקַל֙ הַשִּׁרְי֔וֹן חֲמֵשֶׁת־ אֲלָפִ֥ים שְׁקָלִ֖ים נְחֹֽשֶֽׁת׃ וּמִצְחַ֥ת נְחֹ֖שֶׁת עַל־ רַגְלָ֑יו וְכִיד֥וֹן נְחֹ֖שֶׁת בֵּ֥ין כְּתֵפָֽיו׃

passages.text: The shaft of his spear was like a weaver’s beam, and its iron point weighed six hundred shekels. In addition, his shield bearer went before him.
passages.sermon:
Goliath was a Philistine champion.
He carried a spear.
The shaft of his spear was thick like a weaver’s beam.
The iron point of his spear weighed six hundred shekels.
A man walked in front of Goliath.
This man carried Goliath’s shield.
passages.original: וְחָץ חֲנִית֗וֹ כִּמְנוֹר֙ אֹֽרְגִ֔ים וְלַהֶ֣בֶת חֲנִית֔וֹ שֵׁשׁ־ מֵא֥וֹת שְׁקָלִ֖ים בַּרְזֶ֑ל וְנֹשֵׂ֥א הַצִּנָּ֖ה הֹלֵ֥ךְ לְפָנָֽיו׃

passages.text: And Goliath stood and shouted to the ranks of Israel, “Why do you come out and array yourselves for battle? Am I not a Philistine, and are you not servants of Saul? Choose one of your men and have him come down against me.
passages.sermon:
Goliath was a champion from Gath.
Goliath came out from the Philistine camp.
Goliath stood before the army of Israel.
Goliath shouted to the ranks of Israel.
He said, “Why do you come out to prepare for battle?”
He said, “I am a Philistine.”
He said, “You are servants of Saul.”
He said, “Choose one man from among you.”
He said, “Let him come down to me.”
passages.original: וַֽיַּעֲמֹ֗ד וַיִּקְרָא֙ אֶל־ מַעַרְכֹ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֔ם לָ֥מָּה תֵצְא֖וּ לַעֲרֹ֣ךְ מִלְחָמָ֑ה הֲל֧וֹא אָנֹכִ֣י הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֗י וְאַתֶּם֙ עֲבָדִ֣ים לְשָׁא֔וּל בְּרוּ־ לָכֶ֥ם אִ֖ישׁ וְיֵרֵ֥ד אֵלָֽי׃

passages.text: If he is able to fight me and kill me, then we will be your servants. But if I prevail against him and kill him, then you shall be our servants and labor for us.”
passages.sermon:
Goliath was a Philistine warrior.
He challenged the army of Israel.
He spoke to the Israelites.
He said, “If your man can fight me and kill me, we Philistines will become your servants.
But if I defeat him and kill him, you Israelites will become our servants.
You will serve us.”
passages.original: אִם־ יוּכַ֞ל לְהִלָּחֵ֤ם אִתִּי֙ וְהִכָּ֔נִי וְהָיִ֥ינוּ לָכֶ֖ם לַעֲבָדִ֑ים וְאִם־ אֲנִ֤י אֽוּכַל־ לוֹ֙ וְהִכִּיתִ֔יו וִהְיִ֤יתֶם לָ֙נוּ֙ לַעֲבָדִ֔ים וַעֲבַדְתֶּ֖ם אֹתָֽנוּ׃

passages.text: Then the Philistine said, “I defy the ranks of Israel this day! Give me a man to fight!”
passages.sermon:
Goliath was a Philistine warrior.
He stood before the army of Israel.
He spoke loudly to the Israelites.
He said, “I defy the army of Israel today.
Give me one man.
Let us fight each other.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔י אֲנִ֗י חֵרַ֛פְתִּי אֶת־ מַעַרְכ֥וֹת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה תְּנוּ־ לִ֣י אִ֔ישׁ וְנִֽלָּחֲמָ֖ה יָֽחַד׃

passages.text: On hearing the words of the Philistine, Saul and all the Israelites were dismayed and greatly afraid.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
All the Israelites were his people.
They heard the words of the Philistine.
The Philistine challenged them.
Saul and all the Israelites became dismayed.
They were greatly afraid.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע שָׁאוּל֙ וְכָל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶת־ דִּבְרֵ֥י הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֖י הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַיֵּחַ֥תּוּ וַיִּֽרְא֖וּ מְאֹֽד׃פ

passages.text: Now David was the son of a man named Jesse, an Ephrathite from Bethlehem of Judah who had eight sons in the days of Saul. And Jesse was old and well along in years.
passages.sermon:
David was the son of Jesse.
Jesse was an Ephrathite.
Jesse lived in Bethlehem of Judah.
Jesse had eight sons.
This happened during the days of Saul.
Jesse was old.
Jesse was well along in years.
passages.original: וְדָוִד֩ בֶּן־ אִ֨ישׁ אֶפְרָתִ֜י הַזֶּ֗ה מִבֵּ֥ית לֶ֙חֶם֙ יְהוּדָ֔ה וּשְׁמ֣וֹ יִשַׁ֔י וְל֖וֹ שְׁמֹנָ֣ה בָנִ֑ים וְהָאִישׁ֙ בִּימֵ֣י שָׁא֔וּל זָקֵ֖ן בָּ֥א בַאֲנָשִֽׁים׃

passages.text: The three older sons of Jesse had followed Saul into battle: The firstborn was Eliab, the second was Abinadab, and the third was Shammah.
passages.sermon:
Jesse was the father of several sons.
Jesse had three older sons.
These three older sons followed Saul.
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul went to battle.
The three older sons of Jesse went to battle with Saul.
The name of Jesse’s firstborn son was Eliab.
The name of Jesse’s second son was Abinadab.
The name of Jesse’s third son was Shammah.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֨לְכ֜וּ שְׁלֹ֤שֶׁת בְּנֵֽי־ יִשַׁי֙ הַגְּדֹלִ֔ים הָלְכ֥וּ אַחֲרֵי־ שָׁא֖וּל לַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וְשֵׁ֣ם׀ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת בָּנָ֗יו אֲשֶׁ֤ר הָלְכוּ֙ בַּמִּלְחָמָ֔ה אֱלִיאָ֣ב הַבְּכ֗וֹר וּמִשְׁנֵ֙הוּ֙ אֲבִ֣ינָדָ֔ב וְהַשְּׁלִשִׁ֖י שַׁמָּֽה׃

passages.text: And David was the youngest. The three oldest had followed Saul, but David went back and forth from Saul to tend his father’s sheep in Bethlehem.
passages.sermon:
David was the youngest son of Jesse.
Jesse was from Bethlehem in Judah.
Jesse had eight sons.
The three oldest sons of Jesse followed Saul into battle.
David did not stay with Saul.
David went back and forth from Saul.
David returned home to Bethlehem.
David took care of his father's sheep in Bethlehem.
passages.original: וְדָוִ֖ד ה֣וּא הַקָּטָ֑ן וּשְׁלֹשָׁה֙ הַגְּדֹלִ֔ים הָלְכ֖וּ אַחֲרֵ֥י שָׁאֽוּל׃ס וְדָוִ֛ד הֹלֵ֥ךְ וָשָׁ֖ב מֵעַ֣ל שָׁא֑וּל לִרְע֛וֹת אֶת־ צֹ֥אן אָבִ֖יו בֵּֽית־ לָֽחֶם׃

passages.text: For forty days the Philistine came forward every morning and evening to take his stand.
passages.sermon:
A Philistine man came forward.
He did this every morning.
He did this every evening.
He took his stand each time.
He did this for forty days.
passages.original: וַיִּגַּ֥שׁ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֖י הַשְׁכֵּ֣ם וְהַעֲרֵ֑ב וַיִּתְיַצֵּ֖ב אַרְבָּעִ֥ים יֽוֹם׃פ

passages.text: One day Jesse said to his son David, “Take this ephah of roasted grain and these ten loaves of bread for your brothers and hurry to their camp.
passages.sermon:
Jesse was David’s father.
Jesse spoke to his son David.
Jesse said, “Take this ephah of roasted grain to your brothers.
Take these ten loaves of bread to your brothers.
Hurry to your brothers’ camp.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יִשַׁ֜י לְדָוִ֣ד בְּנ֗וֹ קַח־ נָ֤א לְאַחֶ֙יךָ֙ אֵיפַ֤ת הַקָּלִיא֙ הַזֶּ֔ה וַעֲשָׂרָ֥ה לֶ֖חֶם הַזֶּ֑ה וְהָרֵ֥ץ הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה לְאַחֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Take also these ten portions of cheese to the commander of their unit. Check on the welfare of your brothers and bring back an assurance from them.
passages.sermon:
Jesse was David’s father.
Jesse spoke to his son David.
Jesse gave David instructions.
Jesse said, “Take these ten portions of cheese.”
Jesse told David to bring the cheese to the commander of the unit.
Jesse told David to check on his brothers’ welfare.
Jesse told David to bring back an assurance from his brothers.
passages.original: וְ֠אֵת עֲשֶׂ֜רֶת חֲרִצֵ֤י הֶֽחָלָב֙ הָאֵ֔לֶּה תָּבִ֖יא לְשַׂר־ הָאָ֑לֶף וְאֶת־ אַחֶ֙יךָ֙ תִּפְקֹ֣ד לְשָׁל֔וֹם וְאֶת־ עֲרֻבָּתָ֖ם תִּקָּֽח׃

passages.text: They are with Saul and all the men of Israel in the Valley of Elah, fighting against the Philistines.”
passages.sermon:
Saul is the king of Israel.
All the men of Israel are with Saul.
They are in the Valley of Elah.
They are fighting against the Philistines.
passages.original: וְשָׁא֤וּל וְהֵ֙מָּה֙ וְכָל־ אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בְּעֵ֖מֶק הָֽאֵלָ֑ה נִלְחָמִ֖ים עִם־ פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃

passages.text: So David got up early in the morning, left the flock with a keeper, loaded up, and set out as Jesse had instructed him. He reached the camp as the army was marching out to its position and shouting the battle cry.
passages.sermon:
David was a young shepherd.
Jesse was David’s father.
Jesse gave David instructions.
David got up early in the morning.
David left his flock with a keeper.
David gathered his things.
David set out to follow Jesse’s instructions.
David arrived at the camp.
The army was marching out to its position.
The soldiers were shouting the battle cry.
passages.original: וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֨ם דָּוִ֜ד בַּבֹּ֗קֶר וַיִּטֹּ֤שׁ אֶת־ הַצֹּאן֙ עַל־ שֹׁמֵ֔ר וַיִּשָּׂ֣א וַיֵּ֔לֶךְ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוָּ֖הוּ יִשָׁ֑י וַיָּבֹא֙ הַמַּעְגָּ֔לָה וְהַחַ֗יִל הַיֹּצֵא֙ אֶל־ הַמַּ֣עֲרָכָ֔ה וְהֵרֵ֖עוּ בַּמִּלְחָמָֽה׃

passages.text: And Israel and the Philistines arrayed in formation against each other.
passages.sermon:
Israel stood in formation.
The Philistines also stood in formation.
Israel faced the Philistines.
The Philistines faced Israel.
Both sides prepared to fight each other.
passages.original: וַתַּעֲרֹ֤ךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וּפְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים מַעֲרָכָ֖ה לִקְרַ֥את מַעֲרָכָֽה׃

passages.text: Then David left his supplies in the care of the quartermaster and ran to the battle line. When he arrived, he asked his brothers how they were doing.
passages.sermon:
David was a young shepherd.
David came to the battlefield to visit his brothers.
David carried supplies with him.
David left his supplies with the quartermaster.
David ran to the battle line.
David arrived at the front lines.
David asked his brothers about their well-being.
passages.original: וַיִּטֹּשׁ֩ דָּוִ֨ד אֶת־ הַכֵּלִ֜ים מֵעָלָ֗יו עַל־ יַד֙ שׁוֹמֵ֣ר הַכֵּלִ֔ים וַיָּ֖רָץ הַמַּעֲרָכָ֑ה וַיָּבֹ֕א וַיִּשְׁאַ֥ל לְאֶחָ֖יו לְשָׁלֽוֹם׃

passages.text: And as he was speaking with them, suddenly the champion named Goliath, the Philistine from Gath, came forward from the Philistines and shouted his usual words, which David also heard.
passages.sermon:
David was talking with his brothers.
Goliath came forward from the Philistine army.
Goliath was a champion.
Goliath was a Philistine.
Goliath was from Gath.
Goliath shouted his usual words.
David heard Goliath’s words.
passages.original: וְה֣וּא׀ מְדַבֵּ֣ר עִמָּ֗ם וְהִנֵּ֣ה אִ֣ישׁ הַבֵּנַ֡יִם עוֹלֶ֞ה גָּלְיָת֩ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֨י שְׁמ֤וֹ מִגַּת֙ מִמַּעֲרוֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וַיְדַבֵּ֖ר כַּדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַיִּשְׁמַ֖ע דָּוִֽד׃

passages.text: When all the men of Israel saw Goliath, they fled from him in great fear.
passages.sermon:
The men of Israel saw Goliath.
Goliath was a champion of the Philistines.
He came out from the Philistine army.
When the men of Israel saw him, they ran away from him.
They were very afraid.
passages.original: וְכֹל֙ אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בִּרְאוֹתָ֖ם אֶת־ הָאִ֑ישׁ וַיָּנֻ֙סוּ֙ מִפָּנָ֔יו וַיִּֽירְא֖וּ מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: Now the men of Israel had been saying, “Do you see this man who keeps coming out to defy Israel? To the man who kills him the king will give great riches. And he will give him his daughter in marriage and exempt his father’s house from taxation in Israel.”
passages.sermon:
The men of Israel spoke together.
They said, “Look at this man who comes out again and again.
He comes out to challenge Israel.
He insults us.
Whoever kills him will receive a great reward from the king.
The king will give that man great riches.
The king will give him his daughter as a wife.
The king will make his father’s family free from taxes in Israel.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר׀ אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הַרְּאִיתֶם֙ הָאִ֤ישׁ הָֽעֹלֶה֙ הַזֶּ֔ה כִּ֛י לְחָרֵ֥ף אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עֹלֶ֑ה וְֽ֠הָיָה הָאִ֨ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־ יַכֶּ֜נּוּ יַעְשְׁרֶ֥נּוּ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ׀ עֹ֣שֶׁר גָּד֗וֹל וְאֶת־ בִּתּוֹ֙ יִתֶּן־ ל֔וֹ וְאֵת֙ בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֔יו יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה חָפְשִׁ֖י בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: David asked the men who were standing with him, “What will be done for the man who kills this Philistine and removes this disgrace from Israel? Just who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God?”
passages.sermon:
David stood with the men of Israel.
David spoke to them.
David asked a question.
David said, “What will be done for the man who kills this Philistine?”
David said, “What will be done for the man who removes this disgrace from Israel?”
David called Goliath an uncircumcised Philistine.
David asked, “Who is this uncircumcised Philistine?”
David said, “He defies the armies of the living God.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֗ד אֶֽל־ הָאֲנָשִׁ֞ים הָעֹמְדִ֣ים עִמּוֹ֮ לֵאמֹר֒ מַה־ יֵּעָשֶׂ֗ה לָאִישׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר יַכֶּה֙ אֶת־ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֣י הַלָּ֔ז וְהֵסִ֥יר חֶרְפָּ֖ה מֵעַ֣ל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּ֣י מִ֗י הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֤י הֶֽעָרֵל֙ הַזֶּ֔ה כִּ֣י חֵרֵ֔ף מַעַרְכ֖וֹת אֱלֹהִ֥ים חַיִּֽים׃

passages.text: The people told him about the offer, saying, “That is what will be done for the man who kills him.”
passages.sermon: The people spoke to David.\r\nThey explained the king’s offer.\r\nThey said, “This is what will be done for the man who kills the Philistine.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ הָעָ֔ם כַּדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר כֹּ֣ה יֵעָשֶׂ֔ה לָאִ֖ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַכֶּֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: Now when David’s oldest brother Eliab heard him speaking to the men, his anger burned against David. “Why have you come down here?” he asked. “And with whom did you leave those few sheep in the wilderness? I know your pride and wickedness of heart—you have come down to see the battle!”
passages.sermon:
David was the youngest son of Jesse.
Eliab was David’s oldest brother.
Eliab heard David speaking to the men.
Eliab became very angry with David.
Eliab spoke to David.
Eliab asked, “Why have you come down here?”
Eliab asked, “With whom did you leave those few sheep in the wilderness?”
Eliab said, “I know your pride.”
Eliab said, “I know the evil in your heart.”
Eliab said, “You have come down to see the battle.”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע אֱלִיאָב֙ אָחִ֣יו הַגָּד֔וֹל בְּדַבְּר֖וֹ אֶל־ הָאֲנָשִׁ֑ים וַיִּֽחַר־ אַף֩ אֱלִיאָ֨ב בְּדָוִ֜ד וַיֹּ֣אמֶר׀ לָמָּה־ זֶּ֣ה יָרַ֗דְתָּ וְעַל־ מִ֨י נָטַ֜שְׁתָּ מְעַ֨ט הַצֹּ֤אן הָהֵ֙נָּה֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר אֲנִ֧י יָדַ֣עְתִּי אֶת־ זְדֹנְךָ֗ וְאֵת֙ רֹ֣עַ לְבָבֶ֔ךָ כִּ֗י לְמַ֛עַן רְא֥וֹת הַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה יָרָֽדְתָּ׃

passages.text: “What have I done now?” said David. “Was it not just a question?”
passages.sermon:
David spoke.
David said, “What have I done now?”
David asked, “Was it not just a question?”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֔ד מֶ֥ה עָשִׂ֖יתִי עָ֑תָּה הֲל֖וֹא דָּבָ֥ר הֽוּא׃

passages.text: Then he turned from him toward another and asked about the offer, and those people answered him just as the first ones had answered.
passages.sermon:
David was a young shepherd.
David spoke with the men of Israel.
Eliab was David’s oldest brother.
Eliab became angry with David.
David turned away from Eliab.
David went to another man.
David asked the same question to this man.
The people answered David.
They gave him the same answer as before.
passages.original: וַיִּסֹּ֤ב מֵֽאֶצְלוֹ֙ אֶל־ מ֣וּל אַחֵ֔ר וַיֹּ֖אמֶר כַּדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וַיְשִׁבֻ֤הוּ הָעָם֙ דָּבָ֔ר כַּדָּבָ֖ר הָרִאשֽׁוֹן׃

passages.text: Now David’s words were overheard and reported to Saul, who called for him.
passages.sermon:
David spoke words to the people.
Some people heard what David said.
They reported David’s words to Saul.
Saul heard the report about David.
Saul sent for David and brought him.
passages.original: וַיְּשָּֽׁמְעוּ֙ הַדְּבָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֣ר דָּוִ֑ד וַיַּגִּ֥דוּ לִפְנֵֽי־ שָׁא֖וּל וַיִּקָּחֵֽהוּ׃

passages.text: And David said to Saul, “Let no man’s heart fail on account of this Philistine. Your servant will go and fight him!”
passages.sermon:
David spoke to Saul.
David was a young shepherd.
David said, “Do not let anyone lose heart because of this Philistine.
I am your servant.
I will go.
I will fight this Philistine.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִד֙ אֶל־ שָׁא֔וּל אַל־ יִפֹּ֥ל לֵב־ אָדָ֖ם עָלָ֑יו עַבְדְּךָ֣ יֵלֵ֔ךְ וְנִלְחַ֖ם עִם־ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֥י הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: But Saul replied, “You cannot go out against this Philistine to fight him. You are just a boy, and he has been a warrior from his youth.”
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
David was a young man.
Saul spoke to David.
Saul said, “You cannot go against this Philistine.
You cannot fight him.
You are only a boy.
This Philistine has been a warrior since he was young.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שָׁא֜וּל אֶל־ דָּוִ֗ד לֹ֤א תוּכַל֙ לָלֶ֙כֶת֙ אֶל־ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֣י הַזֶּ֔ה לְהִלָּחֵ֖ם עִמּ֑וֹ כִּֽי־ נַ֣עַר אַ֔תָּה וְה֛וּא אִ֥ישׁ מִלְחָמָ֖ה מִנְּעֻרָֽיו׃ס

passages.text: David replied, “Your servant has been tending his father’s sheep, and whenever a lion or a bear came and carried off a lamb from the flock, I went after it, struck it down, and delivered the lamb from its mouth. If it reared up against me, I would grab it by its fur, strike it down, and kill it.
passages.sermon:
David spoke to Saul.
David said, “I am your servant.
I have watched my father’s sheep.
A lion came.
A bear came.
One of them took a lamb from the flock.
I went after the animal.
I struck it down.
I rescued the lamb from its mouth.
If the animal rose up against me, I grabbed it by its fur.
I struck it again.
I killed it.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִד֙ אֶל־ שָׁא֔וּל רֹעֶ֨ה הָיָ֧ה עַבְדְּךָ֛ לְאָבִ֖יו בַּצֹּ֑אן וּבָ֤א הָֽאֲרִי֙ וְאֶת־ הַדּ֔וֹב וְנָשָׂ֥א שֶׂ֖ה מֵהָעֵֽדֶר׃ וְיָצָ֧אתִי אַחֲרָ֛יו וְהִכִּתִ֖יו וְהִצַּ֣לְתִּי מִפִּ֑יו וַיָּ֣קָם עָלַ֔י וְהֶחֱזַ֙קְתִּי֙ בִּזְקָנ֔וֹ וְהִכִּתִ֖יו וַהֲמִיתִּֽיו׃

passages.text: Your servant has killed lions and bears; this uncircumcised Philistine will be like one of them, for he has defied the armies of the living God.”
passages.sermon:
David spoke to Saul.
David was a young shepherd.
David had protected his father’s sheep.
David said, “I have killed a lion.
I have killed a bear.
I am your servant.
This Philistine is uncircumcised.
He has defied the armies of the living God.
He will be like the lion and the bear.
I will defeat him as I defeated them.”
passages.original: גַּ֧ם אֶֽת־ הָאֲרִ֛י גַּם־ הַדּ֖וֹב הִכָּ֣ה עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ וְֽ֠הָיָה הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֨י הֶעָרֵ֤ל הַזֶּה֙ כְּאַחַ֣ד מֵהֶ֔ם כִּ֣י חֵרֵ֔ף מַעַרְכֹ֖ת אֱלֹהִ֥ים חַיִּֽים׃ס

passages.text: David added, “The LORD, who delivered me from the claws of the lion and the bear, will deliver me from the hand of this Philistine.” “Go,” said Saul, “and may the LORD be with you.”
passages.sermon:
David spoke to Saul.
David was a young shepherd.
David trusted the LORD.
David said, “The LORD saved me from the lion’s paw.
The LORD saved me from the bear’s paw.
The LORD will save me from this Philistine’s hand.”
Saul answered David.
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul said, “Go.
May the LORD be with you.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמֶר֮ דָּוִד֒ יְהוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִצִּלַ֜נִי מִיַּ֤ד הָֽאֲרִי֙ וּמִיַּ֣ד הַדֹּ֔ב ה֣וּא יַצִּילֵ֔נִי מִיַּ֥ד הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֖י הַזֶּ֑הס וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שָׁא֤וּל אֶל־ דָּוִד֙ לֵ֔ךְ וַֽיהוָ֖ה יִהְיֶ֥ה עִמָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: Then Saul clothed David in his own tunic, put a bronze helmet on his head, and dressed him in armor.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
David was a young shepherd.
Saul gave David his own tunic.
Saul put a bronze helmet on David’s head.
Saul dressed David in armor.
passages.original: וַיַּלְבֵּ֨שׁ שָׁא֤וּל אֶת־ דָּוִד֙ מַדָּ֔יו וְנָתַ֛ן ק֥וֹבַע נְחֹ֖שֶׁת עַל־ רֹאשׁ֑וֹ וַיַּלְבֵּ֥שׁ אֹת֖וֹ שִׁרְיֽוֹן׃

passages.text: David strapped his sword over the tunic and tried to walk, but he was not accustomed to them. “I cannot walk in these,” David said to Saul. “I am not accustomed to them.” So David took them off.
passages.sermon:
David was a young shepherd.
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul gave David his own armor and sword.
David put the sword over his tunic.
David tried to walk in the armor and sword.
David was not used to them.
David said to Saul, “I cannot walk in these.”
David said, “I am not accustomed to them.”
David took off the armor and sword.
passages.original: וַיַּחְגֹּ֣ר דָּוִ֣ד אֶת־ חַ֠רְבּוֹ מֵעַ֨ל לְמַדָּ֜יו וַיֹּ֣אֶל לָלֶכֶת֮ כִּ֣י לֹֽא־ נִסָּה֒ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜ד אֶל־ שָׁא֗וּל לֹ֥א אוּכַ֛ל לָלֶ֥כֶת בָּאֵ֖לֶּה כִּ֣י לֹ֣א נִסִּ֑יתִי וַיְסִרֵ֥ם דָּוִ֖ד מֵעָלָֽיו׃

passages.text: And David took his staff in his hand, selected five smooth stones from the brook, and put them in the pouch of his shepherd’s bag. And with his sling in hand, he approached the Philistine.
passages.sermon:
David was a young shepherd.
David faced the Philistine named Goliath.
David took his staff in his hand.
David chose five smooth stones from the brook.
David put the stones in the pouch of his shepherd’s bag.
David held his sling in his hand.
David walked toward the Philistine.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּ֨ח מַקְל֜וֹ בְּיָד֗וֹ וַיִּבְחַר־ ל֣וֹ חֲמִשָּׁ֣ה חַלֻּקֵֽי־ אֲבָנִ֣ים׀ מִן־ הַנַּ֡חַל וַיָּ֣שֶׂם אֹ֠תָם בִּכְלִ֨י הָרֹעִ֧ים אֲשֶׁר־ ל֛וֹ וּבַיַּלְק֖וּט וְקַלְּע֣וֹ בְיָד֑וֹ וַיִּגַּ֖שׁ אֶל־ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּֽי׃

passages.text: Now the Philistine came closer and closer to David, with his shield-bearer before him.
passages.sermon:
The Philistine was a warrior from the enemy army.
He walked toward David.
He came closer to David.
A man walked in front of the Philistine.
This man carried the Philistine’s shield.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֙לֶךְ֙ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔י הֹלֵ֥ךְ וְקָרֵ֖ב אֶל־ דָּוִ֑ד וְהָאִ֛ישׁ נֹשֵׂ֥א הַצִּנָּ֖ה לְפָנָֽיו׃

passages.text: When the Philistine looked and saw David, he despised him because he was just a boy, ruddy and handsome.
passages.sermon:
The Philistine was a warrior and an enemy of Israel.
He looked at David.
He saw David clearly.
David was a young boy.
David had a ruddy complexion.
David was handsome in appearance.
The Philistine despised David.
He despised David because David was only a boy.
He also despised David because David was ruddy and handsome.
passages.original: וַיַּבֵּ֧ט הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֛י וַיִּרְאֶ֥ה אֶת־ דָּוִ֖ד וַיִּבְזֵ֑הוּ כִּֽי־ הָיָ֣ה נַ֔עַר וְאַדְמֹנִ֖י עִם־ יְפֵ֥ה מַרְאֶֽה׃

passages.text: “Am I a dog,” he said to David, “that you come at me with sticks?” And the Philistine cursed David by his gods.
passages.sermon:
The Philistine was a giant warrior.
He spoke to David.
He said, “Am I a dog?”
He saw David coming toward him with sticks.
He asked, “Do you come at me with sticks?”
The Philistine cursed David.
He used the names of his own gods to curse David.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי֙ אֶל־ דָּוִ֔ד הֲכֶ֣לֶב אָנֹ֔כִי כִּֽי־ אַתָּ֥ה בָֽא־ אֵלַ֖י בַּמַּקְל֑וֹת וַיְקַלֵּ֧ל הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֛י אֶת־ דָּוִ֖ד בֵּאלֹהָֽיו׃

passages.text: “Come here,” he called to David, “and I will give your flesh to the birds of the air and the beasts of the field!”
passages.sermon:
The Philistine was a giant warrior and an enemy of Israel.
He spoke to David.
He said, “Come here to me.”
He threatened David.
He said, “I will give your flesh to the birds of the air.”
He also said, “I will give your flesh to the beasts of the field.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֖י אֶל־ דָּוִ֑ד לְכָ֣ה אֵלַ֔י וְאֶתְּנָה֙ אֶת־ בְּשָׂ֣רְךָ֔ לְע֥וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם וּלְבֶהֱמַ֥ת הַשָּׂדֶֽה׃ס

passages.text: But David said to the Philistine, “You come against me with sword and spear and javelin, but I come against you in the name of the LORD of Hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom you have defied.
passages.sermon:
David was a young Israelite.
David faced the Philistine warrior named Goliath.
David spoke to Goliath.
David said, “You come against me with a sword.
You come against me with a spear.
You come against me with a javelin.
I come against you in the name of the LORD of Hosts.
The LORD of Hosts is the God of the armies of Israel.
You have defied the God of Israel.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִד֙ אֶל־ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔י אַתָּה֙ בָּ֣א אֵלַ֔י בְּחֶ֖רֶב וּבַחֲנִ֣ית וּבְכִיד֑וֹן וְאָנֹכִ֣י בָֽא־ אֵלֶ֗יךָ בְּשֵׁם֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֛י מַעַרְכ֥וֹת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר חֵרַֽפְתָּ׃

passages.text: This day the LORD will deliver you into my hand. This day I will strike you down, cut off your head, and give the carcasses of the Philistines to the birds of the air and the creatures of the earth. Then the whole world will know that there is a God in Israel.
passages.sermon:
David spoke to Goliath, the Philistine champion.
David was a young Israelite.
Goliath was a warrior from the Philistine army.
David said, "Today the LORD will give you into my hand."
"Today I will strike you down."
"I will cut off your head."
"I will give the bodies of the Philistine army to the birds of the sky."
"I will give them to the wild animals of the earth."
"Then all the earth will know this truth."
"There is a God in Israel."
passages.original: הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֡ה יְסַגֶּרְךָ֩ יְהוָ֨ה בְּיָדִ֜י וְהִכִּיתִ֗ךָ וַהֲסִרֹתִ֤י אֶת־ רֹֽאשְׁךָ֙ מֵעָלֶ֔יךָ וְנָ֨תַתִּ֜י פֶּ֣גֶר מַחֲנֵ֤ה פְלִשְׁתִּים֙ הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה לְע֥וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם וּלְחַיַּ֣ת הָאָ֑רֶץ וְיֵֽדְעוּ֙ כָּל־ הָאָ֔רֶץ כִּ֛י יֵ֥שׁ אֱלֹהִ֖ים לְיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: And all those assembled here will know that it is not by sword or spear that the LORD saves; for the battle is the LORD’s, and He will give all of you into our hands.”
passages.sermon:
David spoke to the people gathered there.
He wanted everyone present to understand something important.
The LORD does not save by sword.
The LORD does not save by spear.
The LORD is the one who owns the battle.
The LORD will give you into our hands.
passages.original: וְיֵֽדְעוּ֙ כָּל־ הַקָּהָ֣ל הַזֶּ֔ה כִּֽי־ לֹ֛א בְּחֶ֥רֶב וּבַחֲנִ֖ית יְהוֹשִׁ֣יעַ יְהוָ֑ה כִּ֤י לַֽיהוָה֙ הַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וְנָתַ֥ן אֶתְכֶ֖ם בְּיָדֵֽנוּ׃

passages.text: As the Philistine started forward to attack him, David ran quickly toward the battle line to meet him.
passages.sermon:
The Philistine began to move.
He walked forward.
He came closer to David.
David acted quickly.
David ran toward the battle line.
David ran to meet the Philistine.
passages.original: וְהָיָה֙ כִּֽי־ קָ֣ם הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔י וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ וַיִּקְרַ֖ב לִקְרַ֣את דָּוִ֑ד וַיְמַהֵ֣ר דָּוִ֔ד וַיָּ֥רָץ הַמַּעֲרָכָ֖ה לִקְרַ֥את הַפְּלִשְׁתִּֽי׃

passages.text: Then David reached into his bag, took out a stone, and slung it, striking the Philistine on the forehead. The stone sank into his forehead, and he fell facedown on the ground.
passages.sermon:
David was a young shepherd.
David faced the Philistine champion named Goliath.
David reached into his bag.
David took out a stone.
David used his sling.
David slung the stone.
The stone struck the Philistine on the forehead.
The stone sank into the Philistine’s forehead.
The Philistine fell facedown on the ground.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַח֩ דָּוִ֨ד אֶת־ יָד֜וֹ אֶל־ הַכֶּ֗לִי וַיִּקַּ֨ח מִשָּׁ֥ם אֶ֙בֶן֙ וַיְקַלַּ֔ע וַיַּ֥ךְ אֶת־ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֖י אֶל־ מִצְח֑וֹ וַתִּטְבַּ֤ע הָאֶ֙בֶן֙ בְּמִצְח֔וֹ וַיִּפֹּ֥ל עַל־ פָּנָ֖יו אָֽרְצָה׃

passages.text: Thus David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and a stone; without a sword in his hand he struck down the Philistine and killed him.
passages.sermon:
David was a young Israelite.
The Philistine was a giant warrior named Goliath.
David faced the Philistine in battle.
David had a sling and a stone.
David did not have a sword in his hand.
David used the sling and the stone.
David struck the Philistine with the stone.
David killed the Philistine.
passages.original: וַיֶּחֱזַ֨ק דָּוִ֤ד מִן־ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי֙ בַּקֶּ֣לַע וּבָאֶ֔בֶן וַיַּ֥ךְ אֶת־ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֖י וַיְמִיתֵ֑הוּ וְחֶ֖רֶב אֵ֥ין בְּיַד־ דָּוִֽד׃

passages.text: David ran and stood over him. He grabbed the Philistine’s sword and pulled it from its sheath and killed him; and he cut off his head with the sword. When the Philistines saw that their hero was dead, they turned and ran.
passages.sermon:
David was a young Israelite.
Goliath was a Philistine champion.
David ran to Goliath.
David stood over Goliath.
David took Goliath’s sword.
David pulled the sword out of its sheath.
David killed Goliath with the sword.
David cut off Goliath’s head with the sword.
The Philistines saw that their hero was dead.
The Philistines turned and ran away.
passages.original: וַיָּ֣רָץ דָּ֠וִד וַיַּעֲמֹ֨ד אֶל־ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֜י וַיִּקַּ֣ח אֶת־ חַ֠רְבּוֹ וַֽיִּשְׁלְפָ֤הּ מִתַּעְרָהּ֙ וַיְמֹ֣תְתֵ֔הוּ וַיִּכְרָת־ בָּ֖הּ אֶת־ רֹאשׁ֑וֹ וַיִּרְא֧וּ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֛ים כִּֽי־ מֵ֥ת גִּבּוֹרָ֖ם וַיָּנֻֽסוּ׃

passages.text: Then the men of Israel and Judah charged forward with a shout and pursued the Philistines to the entrance of Gath and to the gates of Ekron. And the bodies of the Philistines were strewn along the Shaaraim road to Gath and Ekron.
passages.sermon:
The men of Israel and Judah stood up.
They shouted loudly.
They ran after the Philistines.
They chased them to the entrance of Gath.
They chased them to the gates of Ekron.
Many Philistines died along the way.
Their bodies lay on the road to Shaaraim.
Their bodies lay on the way to Gath.
Their bodies lay on the way to Ekron.
passages.original: וַיָּקֻ֣מוּ אַנְשֵׁי֩ יִשְׂרָאֵ֨ל וִיהוּדָ֜ה וַיָּרִ֗עוּ וַֽיִּרְדְּפוּ֙ אֶת־ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים עַד־ בּוֹאֲךָ֣ גַ֔יְא וְעַ֖ד שַׁעֲרֵ֣י עֶקְר֑וֹן וַֽיִּפְּל֞וּ חַֽלְלֵ֤י פְלִשְׁתִּים֙ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ שַׁעֲרַ֔יִם וְעַד־ גַּ֖ת וְעַד־ עֶקְרֽוֹן׃

passages.text: When the Israelites returned from their pursuit of the Philistines, they plundered their camps.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites chased the Philistines.
The Israelites stopped chasing them.
The Israelites returned from the pursuit.
The Israelites entered the Philistine camps.
The Israelites took things from the Philistine camps.
The Israelites plundered the camps.
passages.original: וַיָּשֻׁ֙בוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִדְּלֹ֖ק אַחֲרֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיָּשֹׁ֖סּוּ אֶת־ מַחֲנֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: David took the head of the Philistine and brought it to Jerusalem, and he put Goliath’s weapons in his own tent.
passages.sermon:
David was a young man from Israel.
David defeated the Philistine champion named Goliath.
David took the head of Goliath.
David brought Goliath’s head to Jerusalem.
David took Goliath’s weapons.
David put Goliath’s weapons in his own tent.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּ֤ח דָּוִד֙ אֶת־ רֹ֣אשׁ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔י וַיְבִאֵ֖הוּ יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְאֶת־ כֵּלָ֖יו שָׂ֥ם בְּאָהֳלֽוֹ׃ס

passages.text: As Saul had watched David going out to confront the Philistine, he said to Abner the commander of the army, “Abner, whose son is this young man?” “As surely as you live, O king,” Abner replied, “I do not know.”
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
David was a young man.
David went out to face the Philistine.
Saul watched David go out.
Abner was the commander of Saul’s army.
Saul spoke to Abner.
Saul said, “Abner, whose son is this young man?”
Abner answered Saul.
Abner said, “As surely as you live, O king, I do not know.”
passages.original: וְכִרְא֨וֹת שָׁא֜וּל אֶת־ דָּוִ֗ד יֹצֵא֙ לִקְרַ֣את הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔י אָמַ֗ר אֶל־ אַבְנֵר֙ שַׂ֣ר הַצָּבָ֔א בֶּן־ מִי־ זֶ֥ה הַנַּ֖עַר אַבְנֵ֑ר וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אַבְנֵ֔ר חֵֽי־ נַפְשְׁךָ֥ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אִם־ יָדָֽעְתִּי׃

passages.text: “Find out whose son this young man is!” said the king.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul spoke to Abner.
Abner was the commander of the army.
Saul said, “Find out whose son this young man is.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ שְׁאַ֣ל אַתָּ֔ה בֶּן־ מִי־ זֶ֖ה הָעָֽלֶם׃ס

passages.text: So when David returned from killing the Philistine, still holding his head in his hand, Abner took him and brought him before Saul.
passages.sermon:
David killed the Philistine.
David returned from the battle.
David still held the Philistine’s head in his hand.
Abner was the commander of Saul’s army.
Abner took David.
Abner brought David before Saul.
passages.original: וּכְשׁ֣וּב דָּוִ֗ד מֵֽהַכּוֹת֙ אֶת־ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔י וַיִּקַּ֤ח אֹתוֹ֙ אַבְנֵ֔ר וַיְבִאֵ֖הוּ לִפְנֵ֣י שָׁא֑וּל וְרֹ֥אשׁ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֖י בְּיָדֽוֹ׃

passages.text: “Whose son are you, young man?” asked Saul. “I am the son of your servant Jesse of Bethlehem,” David replied.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul spoke to David.
Saul said, “Whose son are you, young man?”
David answered Saul.
David said, “I am the son of your servant Jesse.”
David said, “Jesse is from Bethlehem.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ שָׁא֔וּל בֶּן־ מִ֥י אַתָּ֖ה הַנָּ֑עַר וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֔ד בֶּֽן־ עַבְדְּךָ֥ יִשַׁ֖י בֵּ֥ית הַלַּחְמִֽי׃
